events.title: Japanese BBQ Meetup 🔥
events.description: Monthly BBQ at My Khe Beach! Bring your own drinks, we provide the grill and meat. Great chance to meet other Japanese expats in a relaxed setting. First-timers very welcome!

events.title: Morning Cafe Meetup ☕
events.description: Casual morning coffee and chat. We meet every other Sunday at Cong Cafe. Come say hi!

events.title: Son Tra Peninsula Hike 🥾
events.description: Moderate hike up Son Tra peninsula. Amazing ocean views and monkey spotting. Bring water and sunscreen.

events.title: JP-VN Exchange Dinner 🍽️
events.description: Japanese-Vietnamese cultural exchange dinner. Try local dishes and practice Vietnamese with friendly locals!

threadDetail.title: Any places to go alone on weekends?
threadDetail.author: senpai-003
threadDetail.body: I've been in Da Nang for about a month now. Work is fine, but weekends are really lonely. My colleagues go home to their families. Does anyone know good spots for a solo expat on weekends? Cafes, parks, activities... anything helps!

replies.author: senpai-002
replies.text: My Khe Beach is great on Saturday mornings — get there before 7am for sunrise. Also check the events page — there's a BBQ this Saturday! I organize it monthly. Come join us 🔥

replies.author: senpai-001
replies.text: Son Tra peninsula hike is amazing solo — I go every other Sunday. The views from the top are incredible. Also, Cong Cafe in Hai Chau is a great spot for a chill afternoon with a good book.

replies.author: user-new-001
replies.text: I'm also new here! Only been 2 weeks. Following this thread. Let's hang out sometime? 😊

replies.author: senpai-004
replies.text: Dragon Bridge fire show on Saturday night is a must-see! Also the Han Market area is fun to explore solo. If you like working out, there are some cheap gyms around Son Tra area.

areas.name: Hai Chau
areas.description: The heart of Da Nang — central location with easy access to restaurants, shops, and offices. Most popular area for expats who work in the city center.

areas.name: Son Tra
areas.description: Peaceful coastal district with beautiful beaches and mountain views. Popular among expats who value quality of life and don't mind a short commute.

areas.name: Ngu Hanh Son
areas.tagline: My Khe Beach area, tourist zone
areas.description: Home to the famous My Khe Beach strip with luxury resorts and tourist amenities. Good for those who enjoy beach lifestyle with modern facilities.

areas.name: East of Han River
areas.description: The authentic local side of Da Nang. Lower prices, real Vietnamese neighborhood feel, and excellent street food. Best value for budget-conscious expats.
pros: Quick bridge crossing to Hai Chau

listings.title: Ocean View 1BR Apartment — Son Tra
listings.description: Bright, furnished 1BR with stunning ocean view. Rooftop pool and modern gym. Quiet neighborhood, 5-min walk to My Khe Beach.

listings.title: Modern Studio — Hai Chau Center
listings.description: Cozy studio in the heart of Hai Chau. Walking distance to offices, restaurants, and convenience stores. Perfect for solo professionals.

listings.title: Spacious 2BR Family Apartment — Son Tra
listings.description: Family-friendly 2BR with large balcony and mountain views. Quiet building with playground. Available from May 1st.

listings.title: Budget-Friendly 1BR — East of Han River
listings.description: Affordable 1BR in a local neighborhood. Great street food nearby. Basic but clean and well-maintained.

listings.title: Luxury 1BR — Ngu Hanh Son Beach
listings.description: Premium beachfront apartment with infinity pool and full resort amenities. Direct beach access. Ideal for those wanting luxury lifestyle.

listings.title: Cozy Studio Near Dragon Bridge — Hai Chau
listings.description: Small but well-located studio right next to Dragon Bridge. Perfect for short stays or budget-conscious newcomers.

senpai.name: Yuki Yamamoto
senpai.bio: Moved to Da Nang for work in 2024. Love the beach life and local food scene.
senpai.quote: Moving to Son Tra was the best decision. 5-min walk to the beach!

senpai.name: Takeshi Sato
senpai.bio: Opened a Japanese restaurant in Hai Chau. Know every corner of this city.
senpai.quote: Hai Chau is where the action is. Everything you need within walking distance.

senpai.name: Mika Suzuki
senpai.bio: Teaching English at a local school. Da Nang feels like home now.
senpai.quote: Housing was my biggest challenge too. The key is to decide the area first!

senpai.name: Kenji Watanabe
senpai.bio: Digital nomad who fell in love with Da Nang and decided to stay.
senpai.quote: The cost of living here is amazing. I pay half of what I did in Tokyo for twice the space.

reviews.author: senpai-001
reviews.text: Furnished and move-in ready. The landlord speaks English and handles repairs quickly. Some noise from the street but at this price, very satisfied.

reviews.author: senpai-004
reviews.text: Great location and view. Pool is nice but small. WiFi is fast enough for video calls. Would recommend for solo professionals.

reviews.author: senpai-003
reviews.text: Perfect for my first month in Da Nang. Small but has everything you need. Convenience store downstairs is super handy.
